papers.title_en: Reinforcement Learning from Intermediate Renders for Image-to-Code Generation
papers.authors: Omri Kaduri, Kate Feingold, Phillip Isola, Tali Dekel
papers.evidence: 视觉语言模型生成SVG代码并利用中间渲染奖励
papers.tldr: 图像到代码生成的强化学习后训练通常只依赖最终渲染奖励，反馈稀疏且难与单个 token 的贡献对齐。IR4RL 观察到中间代码前缀常可执行并产生有意义的局部渲染，于是把相邻中间渲染的变化转化为 token 级进度奖励。在 Image-to-SVG 与 Image-to-TikZ 上，该方法优于监督微调和标准 GRPO，刷新开源模型最优结果。这表明中间渲染可作为简单有效的过程监督信号。
papers.abstract_en: Reinforcement learning is increasingly used to post-train vision-language models for image-to-code generation, such as generating SVG code from a reference image, by optimizing rewards computed from the final rendered output. However, relying on a single terminal reward provides sparse feedback that is poorly aligned with the contribution of individual tokens. A generated program may contain operations that accurately reproduce some parts of the target image alongside others that introduce errors, yet all tokens are trained from the same final outcome. We observe that many intermediate code prefixes are not only executable, but already produce meaningful partial renders that reflect progress toward the target. This property provides a natural source of denser supervision during generation. Based on this observation, we introduce IR4RL, an RL framework with a token-level render-progress reward that turns changes between intermediate renders into localized feedback for the generated sequence. We evaluate our approach on Image-to-SVG and Image-to-TikZ generation. Across both tasks, our method improves over supervised fine-tuning and standard GRPO, yielding new state-of-the-art open-source models. This shows that intermediate rendering provides a simple and effective source of process supervision for RL post-training of image-to-code models.

papers.title_en: DrawingsDreamer: A Unified Multi-View Engineering Drawings Generation Model
papers.authors: Shurui Liu, Weide Chen, Changwang Yi, Ancong Wu
papers.evidence: 以序列建模和分层词元化驱动大模型生成SVG矢量图形
papers.tldr: 现有自回归 SVG 生成模型多面向艺术创作，难以满足工程图所需的严格几何保真与跨视图空间对齐。DrawingsDreamer 将多视图矢量工程图生成统一建模为序列任务，无需栅格图像编码器，并采用分层后缀标记化与渐进式任务感知课程。实验表明其在多种条件与无条件生成中兼顾几何保真和语法准确。该工作为 CAD 多视图工程图自动生成提供了统一框架。
papers.abstract_en: Scalable Vector Graphics (SVG) are essential for modern industrial Computer-Aided Design (CAD). However, existing autoregressive SVG generation models are predominantly tailored for artistic creation and struggle to maintain the rigorous geometric fidelity and cross-view spatial alignment required for engineering drawings. To bridge this gap, we introduce \textbf{DrawingsDreamer}, a unified Large Language Model (LLM)-driven framework for multi-view vector-based engineering drawings generation. By formulating the generation of multi-view engineering drawings purely as a sequence modeling task, we eliminate the need of raster image encoders. We propose a Streamlined Representation utilizing hierarchical postfix tokenization, which guides the model to establish local geometric coordinates before assigning semantic boundaries. Optimized via a progressive task-aware curriculum schedule, \textbf{DrawingsDreamer} effectively transitions from localized structural repair to macroscopic generation in a unified model. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our unified model achieves strong performance in both geometric fidelity and syntactic accuracy across diverse conditional and unconditional generation tasks.

papers.title_en: Code2Video-Compass: A Comprehensive Benchmark for General-Purpose Code-Based Video Generation across T2V, I2V, and V2V
papers.authors: Zhenghan Chen, Zekai Shao, Xin Lin, Leting Cheng, Siming Chen
papers.evidence: 多模态大模型将视觉与时间需求转写为可执行程序以生成视频
papers.tldr: 代码化视频生成具备精细控制与可编辑优势，但现有基准多聚焦专用任务，缺乏对完整创作和多输入模态的系统评估。为此提出 Code2Video-Compass，覆盖 T2V、I2V、V2V，含 2,104 个任务、10 类、24 子类及三维复杂度。它结合 12 项客观与 5 项主观指标，评测 15 个来自 9 个家族的 MLLM。结果显示领先模型仍难稳定生成高质量完整视频，且性能随构建、动态动画和状态依赖复杂度上升而下降，为可靠可控的代码化视频生成提供统一评测。
papers.abstract_en: Code-based video generation offers fine-grained control, targeted editing, and component reuse compared with direct video generation. This approach requires multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to translate visual and temporal requirements into executable programs that produce complete videos. However, existing code-based benchmarks primarily target specialized tasks, leaving complete video creation across diverse creative categories and input modalities insufficiently evaluated. We introduce Code2Video-Compass, a general-purpose benchmark for code-based video generation across text-to-video (T2V), image-to-video (I2V), and video-to-video (V2V) settings. Code2Video-Compass comprises 2,104 tasks spanning 10 categories, 24 subtypes, and three complexity dimensions covering construction, dynamic animation, and state dependency. It combines tasks curated from textual instructions and visual references with corresponding T2V, I2V, and V2V tasks derived from complete professional and user-created videos. We propose a dual-level evaluation framework combining 12 objective metrics and five subjective metrics. Objective evaluation covers operational performance, video quality, text-video alignment, and reference fidelity, while subjective evaluation uses an MLLM judge to evaluate instruction following and holistic video quality. Extensive evaluation of 15 recent proprietary and open-weight MLLMs from nine families reveals that even leading models face challenges in reliably generating high-quality complete videos aligned with textual and visual requirements, with performance generally declining as construction, dynamic animation, and state-dependency complexity increases. We anticipate that Code2Video-Compass will advance reliable, coherent, and controllable code-based video generation and inspire broader progress in programmatic visual creation.

papers.title_en: MaLiang-Harness: A Programmable Path to Image and Video Generation
papers.authors: Haoyu Zhao, Zihao Zhang, Xudong Wang, Jiaxi Gu, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang, Shuicheng Yan
papers.evidence: 多模态大模型驱动的可执行程序化视觉生成与修订
papers.tldr: 可执行程序能显式控制图像与视频构建，但代码执行正确并不等于满足构图、外观或运动要求，作者将这一差异定义为 P2V gap。MaLiang-Harness 将 MLLM 驱动的视觉生成组织为持续构建、检查与修订流程，并以 PEG 状态、TGP 轨迹和 REV 修订验证共享同一修订参照。在 MaLiang-IBench 与 MaLiang-VBench 上，GPT-6-Astra 生成成功率达 100%，图像与视频质量全达标比例分别为 96.0% 和 76.9%。该工作为研究程序化生成及通用基准预测局限提供系统基础。
papers.abstract_en: Executable programs offer explicit control over how images and videos are constructed, but generating runnable code is only the beginning of visual creation. A program can execute correctly while violating the requested composition, appearance, or motion. We define this discrepancy as the Program-to-Visual (P2V) gap and introduce MaLiang-Harness, a unified framework for organizing MLLM-driven visual generation into a persistent process of construction, inspection, and revision. Its central design is to make the evolving visual program, its construction history, and its verification share a common revision reference. We define the Persistent Executable Generation (PEG) state as preserving programs and task context. Traceable Generation Process (TGP) connects edits to rendered evidence, and Revision-aware Editing and Verification (REV) supports restoration and checks the current revision before completion. Together, these mechanisms coordinate planning, execution, and visual feedback across rendering backends. We evaluate 11 powerful closed-source MLLMs on MaLiang-IBench and four on MaLiang-VBench, measuring generation success, visual quality, and computational cost. GPT-6-Astra achieves 100% generation success on both benchmarks, with 96.0% of image tasks and 76.9% of video tasks meeting all quality thresholds. The comparison also reveals a mismatch between general capability scores and visual generation performance, with similarly scored models differing substantially in their ability to satisfy visual requirements. MaLiang-Harness provides a systematic basis for studying how MLLMs translate executable code into visual outcomes, exposing both the potential of programmable generation and the limitations of general benchmarks as predictors of this ability. The project is available at https://github.com/gulucaptain/MaLiang-Harness.
